Nimbus is an operator authorized by the National Civil Aviation Authority (ENAC) and is inscribed under the Italian Federation of Aerospace, Defense and Security (AIAD). Besides, since his home-made products and licenses, Nimbus SRL is one of the companies that joins “Exclusive Brand Torino”, an institution that gather the most innovative companies in Piemonte. 
Moreover, Nimbus has been certified as a recognized entity by ENAV (Italian Civil Aviation Authority) and has been authorized to operate as an examination center (OPEN A2 ONLINE PROCTORED) for the issue of the UAS Remote Pilot Competence Certificate in the OPEN A2 subcategory, as required by Reg. (EU) no. 2019/947. 
Nimbus’s team consists of high-qualified mechanical, mechatronic, SW, electronic and aerospace engineer, which designed and produced our Nimbus PPL series 418 (quadcopter), Nimbus 612 EVO Plus XL (esacopter) – also with DDSS configuration - the “Nimbus VTOL” and the “Nimbus box”. 
Our UAS can address different scenarios, as visible-light video footage, visual and infra- red survey, structural analysis of industrial construction, agro-tech activities, VOR and ILS operations in airport facilities, high-voltage power lines inspections, delivery activities in the healthcare sector and many others. 
Our professional UAS are distinguished from the rest of the market for the construction and for the flight management features that meet the active and passive safety priorities: the use of soft material, propeller protection, no sharp edges, four/six dual- power motors, proprietary electronics with in-flight safety and emergency management controls. 
Moreover, they are equipped with pilot stations made by two remote commands (main and secondary), which are fitted with telemetry station and PC dedicated to control:
- the remote pilot aircraft;
- the different Payload typologies.

The
Environmental Protection Agency of Aosta Valley (ARPAVdA) is a
multidisciplinary agency dedicated to environment protection and
monitoring (air and water quality, soil contamination, environmental
noise, waste, resources management, renewable energies, ...). Since
2003 ARPAVdA has structured a research unit focused on Climate Change
Impacts on the mountains. The Climate Change Unit conducts studies on
the cryosphere and the biosphere based on the integration of field
observations, remote sensing, and modeling. Considering the
cryosphere, ARPAVdA research activities are focused on glacier mass
balance, snow hydrology (snow water equivalent modeling at regional
and watershed-scale) and permafrost (thermal state monitoring, rock
glaciers movements). Considering the biosphere ARPAVdA works on
ecosystem carbon balance, ecosystem response to climate
change/extremes and vegetation phenology. In particular, ARPAVdA runs
a CO2 flux site (IT-Tor) belonging to the ICOS (www.icos-ri.eu/) and
Fluxnet (fluxnet.fluxdata.org/) networks. ARPAVdA observation sites
contribute to several international networks like GLORIA, LTER,
GTN-P, Phenocam,…. Since the last five years, ARPAVdA is also
devoted to the analysis of climate change impacts on socio-economic
sectors (such as agriculture, tourism, natural resources management,
...) Since several years CCU is collaborating with international
research groups as well as local stakeholders (protected areas, NGOs,
…). ARPA VdA is highly active and successful in acquiring external
funding from national and international sources. Concerning EU
programs, since 2008 ARPAVdA has been involved in more than 30
European funded Projects (Interreg, Life, FP7, ..).

With its personalized approach, Nueva Mater Dei increases the quality of life of its residents significantly. From rehabilitation services to memory care, their residents reap the benefits of having a compassionate and resourceful staff that caters to their every need. Careful interior design gives an elegant but homely feel, which is comfortable and friendly. Study and analyse the emergence of innovative ICT-based products, services and systems for ageing well and managing chronic diseases, including innovative systems to control the COVID-19.
We are active in the wider world of active and healthy ageing, and have many partnerships across the sector that support older people and help to increase activity in the healthy ageing market.

entityDescription:
FullBrand was born as a spin-off of Little Bull of the Armando Testa group to design and implement marketing and communication strategies based on Brand Experience and Brand Innovation. Through Brand Experience services, FullBrand develops an alternative communication to the traditional Above the line approach, coordinating the different languages to use, creating and producing content. Through Brand Innovation services, FullBrand imagines, designs and creates prototypes of products or services for its customers according to its Innovation model defined Application Transfer. FullBrand has offices in Italy and Brazil. Fullbrand has already developed several solutions using proprietary and open source AR and VR Technologies, for immersive reality devices and stereoscopic monitors, in single player or multi-user mode, using gamification techniques. Fullbrand is focused on developing VR and AR solutions for staff training and is developing its experience in telemedicine applications.
From 2016 until today, in collaboration with the Municipality of Sestriere (Turin) we have provided telemedicine services to residents and tourists of a mountain centre located at 2,000 metres, which passes from a resident population of less than a thousand to a population of 35,000 during the winter holidays and which is 45 minutes from the first hospital. After these years of experience in the sector, the conclusion is that the solution for the current needs of the Health Service is not Telemedicine as such, but the virtualization of the health service of which telemedicine is one of the tools. The exclusively telemedicine approach is ideological, that of virtualization is concrete. Virtualization minimizes the infrastructure and works on all possibilities, like a pianist on the piano keyboard. Virtualization is necessary because the superstructure has become predominant over the structure and is suffocating it. It is a matter of managing the health resources needed to provide the service where it is needed, focusing on prevention (e.g. mass dermatological examinations) and self-organization of subjects (e.g. non-competitive sports medicine examinations promoted by mothers). Sestriere's experience has made this clear. We must not have the taboo of a direct visit. Because what we have shown is how service management virtualization works in terms of service delivery. This trend is perfectly in line with the general virtualization of services. In commerce (and Amazon proves it) all channels are used to provide the user with the best service at the best price.

Thanks for this granular management of the network resources, our frameworks have been widely deployed at Universities, Governments and Health Organizations worldwide, by assuring their operativity even in the most demanding operational scenarios.
